Prove the conjunction componentwise.

- For the two-valued time \(\tau=\mathbf 1_s\,i+\mathbf 1_{s^c}\,j\), fix \(k\). Using \(i\le j\), the event \(\{\tau\le k\}\) is either \(\varnothing\), \(s\), or \(\Omega\). In the only nontrivial case, \(i\le k\), so measurability of \(s\) propagates from \(\mathcal G_i\) to \(\mathcal G_k\) by monotonicity of the filtration. This verifies the stopping-time criterion.

- For the second component, use the representation
  \[
  \{\tau<i\}=\bigcup_{j<i}\{\tau\le j\}.
  \]
  Each event \(\{\tau\le j\}\) is measurable in the stopped measurable space: when intersected with \(\{\tau\le k\}\), it becomes
  \[
  \{\tau\le \min(j,k)\},
  \]
  which is measurable at time \(\min(j,k)\) by the stopping-time hypothesis and hence at time \(k\) by filtration monotonicity. Finally, `Countable ι` turns the displayed union into a countable union of stopped-measurable sets.

The essential assumptions are the linear order, used through \(\min(j,k)\), and countability, needed for the union over all \(j<i\).
